::: {#sol-gru-pixels}

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
pixel_gru = make_reader(nn.GRU, 1)
_ = train(pixel_gru, n_epochs=20)
gru_acc = accuracy(pixel_gru)
print(gru_acc)
# The prose below says both gated readers beat both plain ones; stop if not.
assert min(gru_acc, lstm_acc) > max(pixel_acc, clipped_acc)
```

| Layer reading the pixels | [Gradient clipping](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/backpropagation.html#def-gradient-clipping) | Test [accuracy](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/metrics.html#def-accuracy) |
|:--|:--|--:|
| `nn.RNN` | None | `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * py$pixel_acc)` |
| `nn.RNN` | To 1 | `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * py$clipped_acc)` |
| `nn.LSTM` | None | `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * py$lstm_acc)` |
| `nn.GRU` | None | `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * py$gru_acc)` |

The [GRU](#def-gru) reader classifies `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * py$gru_acc)` of the test digits correctly,
`r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * abs(py$gru_acc - py$lstm_acc))` percentage points `r if (py$gru_acc > py$lstm_acc) "above" else "below"` the [LSTM](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/cnn-rnn.html#def-lstm) reader,
with `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * py$gru_count / py$lstm_count)` as many [parameters](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/big-ideas.html#def-parameter) in its [recurrent layer](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/cnn-rnn.html#def-recurrent-layer).
`r if (abs(py$gru_acc - py$lstm_acc) < 0.01) "So the GRU reader is about as accurate, not more." else if (py$gru_acc > py$lstm_acc) "So the GRU reader is more accurate." else "So the GRU reader is less accurate."`
Both gated readers beat the plain recurrent readers.
On other tasks,
@chung2014empirical found neither gated layer consistently better than the other.

:::
